stats.description: Track your training volume, distance, pace and heart rate over time.
stats.empty: No activities for the selected sport and year.
stats.noHeartRate: No saved heart rate data during this period.
stats.chartScale: Scale: 0–{{max}}. All values are in the table below.
stats.method: Time includes pauses. Pace is total time per kilometre for activities with distance and time. Lower pace means faster speed. Heart rate is weighted by activity duration, using only activities with saved heart rate. Missing values appear as –. All sports also combines pace and heart rate across sports. Months follow your device’s time zone.

yearComparison.title: Year over year
yearComparison.description: Accumulated volume per year on the same calendar, for the selected sport.
yearComparison.chart: Accumulated {{metric}} per year. The selected year is highlighted.
yearComparison.empty: No activities for the selected sport.
yearComparison.method: The chart shows the selected year and up to {{years}} most recent years. The comparison uses the same month and day each year, and the change compares with the year before. Time includes pauses, and each activity counts on the day it starts in your device's time zone.

trainingLoad.title: Training load
trainingLoad.description: Fitness, fatigue and form from your runs, calculated from pace against your threshold pace.
trainingLoad.thresholdManual: You have set your threshold pace yourself.
trainingLoad.thresholdPredicted: Automatically {{pace}} /km from your prediction. Set your own if you know better.
trainingLoad.thresholdMissing: No prediction yet. Set your threshold pace, or run 5 km or longer with distance data.
trainingLoad.empty: No runs to calculate load from yet.
trainingLoad.method: One hour at threshold pace gives a load of 100; load grows with the square of speed. Speed is smoothed over 30 seconds and pauses do not count. Activities without a file are estimated from average pace. Fitness is the average daily load over about 42 days, fatigue over 7 days and form the difference. Threshold pace is the pace you can hold for an hour, derived from VDOT unless you set it yourself, and applies to your whole history. Hills are not adjusted for yet. Only running counts.
trainingLoad.warningText: Your fitness has increased by {{ramp}} in a week. A common rule of thumb is at most about 7 per week; an easier period lowers the risk of overload.

records.help: Does something look wrong? You can exclude an activity with incorrect data from running records by editing the activity.
records.title: Running records
records.description: Best efforts from your runs with recorded data from a file. Time includes pauses.
records.empty: No records yet. Records come from runs uploaded from a file with distance data.
records.trendChart: Best time per month over {{distance}}. Faster times are higher.
records.chartScale: Fastest at the top: {{best}}, slowest at the bottom: {{worst}}.
records.chartScaleHint: The scale follows personal bests. Monthly bests are shown within that range.
records.predictionsEmpty: No prediction yet. It needs an effort of 5 km or longer in the last 90 days.
records.predictionsMethod: The prediction uses Jack Daniels and Jimmy Gilbert's VDOT formulas, based on your strongest effort of 5 km or longer in the last 90 days. It assumes you have trained for the distance; a marathon takes endurance that a shorter effort does not show. Efforts within training runs are often slower than races.

settings.title: Settings
settings.importWait: The import runs on the server. You can leave this page and come back; progress is shown here.
settings.importHelp: Choose the complete ZIP export, up to 500 MB. Shoes are imported first and linked to activities to calculate distance and time per shoe. Names, summaries and available streams are imported. Heart rate follows your choice above. You can retry after an interruption; duplicates are skipped. Find your imported activities under Activities.
settings.importEquipmentResult: Shoes imported: {{imported}}. Existing activities linked to shoes: {{linked}}.
settings.failedImports: Strava IDs of activities that could not be imported
settings.exportHelp: Download a ZIP with your activities as JSON, including streams, laps, tags and equipment, along with your profile and best efforts. Saved original files are included. Manual activities have no original file, and files that were not saved or were deleted when heart rate consent was withdrawn cannot be exported. Your hidden places are also included.
settings.exportWait: This may take several minutes. Keep this page open until the download starts.
settings.recalculateHelp: Recalculates records and training load for all your activities with recorded data, for example after the calculations have improved. Your activities and their measurements are not changed. It runs on the server and you can leave the page.
